# 1 Samuel Chapter 31 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 168r–168v | **Source Image:** 1SA_031_page_001.jpg, 1SA_031_page_002.jpg

---

**31:1** And-[the]-Philistines [were]-fighting against-Israel, and-fled [the]-men of-Israel from-before [the]-Philistines, and-fell slain on-Mount Gilboa.

**31:2** And-overtook [the]-Philistines Saul and-his-sons, and-struck [the]-Philistines Jonathan and-Abinadab and-Malchi-shua, sons of-Saul.

**31:3** And-was-heavy the-battle against-Saul, and-found-him the-archers, men [with]-the-bow, and-he-was-very-wounded [va-yachel me'od] from-the-archers.

**31:4** And-said Saul to-his-armor-bearer, "Draw your-sword and-thrust-me-through with-it, lest come these uncircumcised-ones and-thrust-me-through and-deal-ruthlessly with-me [ve-hit'alelu vi]." But-his-armor-bearer was-not-willing, for he-feared exceedingly. And-took Saul the-sword and-fell upon-it.

**31:5** And-saw his-armor-bearer that Saul [was]-dead, and-fell also-he upon his-sword and-died with-him.

**31:6** And-died Saul and-his-three sons and-his-armor-bearer, also all his-men, on-that day together.

**31:7** And-saw the-men of-Israel who [were]-across the-valley and-who [were]-across the-Jordan that the-men of-Israel had-fled and-that Saul and-his-sons [were]-dead, and-they-abandoned the-cities and-fled. And-came [the]-Philistines and-dwelt in-them.

**31:8** And-it-was on-the-next-day, and-came [the]-Philistines to-strip the-slain, and-they-found Saul and-his-three sons fallen on-Mount Gilboa.

**31:9** And-they-cut-off his-head and-stripped his-armor, and-sent [them] into-[the]-land of-[the]-Philistines round-about, to-bring-good-news [le-vasser] [to the]-house of-their-idols and-the-people.

**31:10** And-they-put his-armor [in the]-house of-Ashtaroth, and-his-body they-fastened on-[the]-wall of-Beth-shan.

**31:11** And-heard concerning-him the-inhabitants of-Jabesh-gilead [that]-which [the]-Philistines had-done to-Saul.

**31:12** And-arose all [the]-men of-valor and-walked all the-night and-took the-body of-Saul and-the-bodies of-his-sons from-[the]-wall of-Beth-shan, and-came to-Jabesh and-burned them there.

**31:13** And-they-took their-bones and-buried [them] under the-tamarisk-tree [eshel] in-Jabesh, and-fasted seven days.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **31:3 — va-yachel me'od**: "He was very wounded/terrified" — the root *ch-y-l* can mean both "to writhe in pain" and "to tremble in fear." The ambiguity may be deliberate.

2. **31:4 — ve-hit'alelu vi**: "Deal ruthlessly with me" — literally "make sport of me." Saul fears the humiliation of capture more than death itself.

3. **31:9 — le-vasser**: "To bring good news" — the same root (*b-s-r*) used for good news/gospel. The Philistines send Saul's head and armor to announce their victory to their gods and people.

4. **31:11-13 — Jabesh-gilead's loyalty**: The men of Jabesh-gilead risk their lives to recover Saul's body — repaying his deliverance of their city in ch.11. This act of hesed bookends Saul's story: his reign began saving Jabesh-gilead and ends with their devotion to his remains.

5. **31:13 — eshel**: "Tamarisk tree" — the same word used for the tree under which Saul held court in 22:6. His burial beneath a tamarisk creates a poignant echo.

— EMET
